title: Commercial ratecard delegation and SQ‑triggered pricing playbook
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Goal: Create an operational playbook that (1) centralizes a canonical commercial ratecard, (2) defines delegation thresholds for discount approvals across roles, and (3) declares explicit triggers from Security Questionnaires (SQ) that route deals into escalations or special T&Cs.

Background: We currently have inconsistent ad-hoc discounts and delayed SQ escalations that slow enterprise closures and increase compliance risk. This playbook should speed approvals for standard mid-market deals while ensuring high-risk contracts receive proper legal/security review.

Scope:
- Build a single source-of-truth ratecard (list prices, add-on packaging, renewal guidance, meter units).
- Define role-based delegation thresholds (AE, AM, Sales Director, Head of Commercial, CFO signoff thresholds).
- Define clear SQ triggers (data residency, on-prem, encryption/KMS requirements, SOC2 gap, SIEM integration, HIPAA, FedRAMP scope, include PII/PHI handling, >$500k ARR).
- Define the workflow integrated with CRM (deal fields, approval status, SQ flag, automated Slack alerts to deal-desk channel).
- Telemetry and audit: capture decision metadata (who approved, reason code, date) and feed into pricing dashboards.
- Training + change management for Sales, Legal, RevOps, Solutions Engineering.

Proposed delegation matrix (draft):
- AE (quota-carrying seller): can approve non-binding deal credits up to 10% or $25k ACV, whichever lower.
- AM (account manager): up to 15% or $75k ACV.
- Sales Director: up to 25% or $250k ACV.
- Head of Commercial: up to 35% or $1M ACV with documented commercial rationale.
- CFO/CEO/Legal: discounts >35% or multi-year commitments with custom legal clauses or where on-prem/VPC is requested.

SQ triggers (example rules):
- Auto-escalate if: customer requests on-prem install, required KMS/HSM integration, HIPAA or other regulated data handling, FedRAMP/AICPA-specified scope, or if the SQ contains any specific redlines in encryption/audit clauses.
- Revenue trigger: deals >$500k ARR should always surface to Legal + Security for review.

Acceptance criteria:
- Ratecard published in Confluence and linked from deal desk in CRM.
- Delegation thresholds implemented as validation rules in CRM with automated approval flows where possible.
- SQ triggers wire up to support ticketing and alerting (incidents created for Legal/Security review).
- Audit log of approvals created and visible in pricing dashboard.
- At least two trainings run for Sales and RevOps with >80% attendance by quota-bearing sellers.

Rollout phases:
- Phase 0 (2 weeks): finalize thresholds with Finance & Legal; prototype CRM fields.
- Phase 1 (3 weeks): implement validation rules, approval flows, and telemetry.
- Phase 2 (2 weeks): train, pilot with two ARR segments, iterate off feedback.
- Phase 3: full roll out and enforcement.

Risks & mitigations:
- Pushback from Sales on reduced flexibility -> provide fast path for documented exceptions and an appeals path via Deal Desk.
- Workflow gaps in older CRM instances -> RevOps will provide scripts and manual fallback.
- SQ variance across customers -> provide standardized SQ response snippets and a lightweight triage checklist.

Stakeholders: Sales (Revenue Ops), Legal, Security, Finance, RevOps, Solutions Engineering, Customer Success, Product (PM).

Next steps (immediate):
1) Sync with Legal & Security (this week) to finalize SQ trigger list.
2) RevOps to draft CRM validation rules and sample deal stages.
3) Create Confluence canonical ratecard for review and feedback.
